headline: Stripe will reportedly acquire AI gateway startup OpenRouter for over $7B
summary: The reported acquisition price of over $7 billion for the AI gateway startup OpenRouter marks a significant jump from its $1.3 billion valuation just last May.
details: Stripe has reportedly finalized a deal to acquire OpenRouter, an AI gateway startup, according to a new report by Bloomberg. The acquisition price is said to be over $7 billion, marking a significant move in the AI sector.

OpenRouter specializes in helping customers select various AI models based on their specific needs and budget. The company had previously raised a $113 million Series B round in May, at a reported valuation of $1.3 billion.

OpenRouter's CEO, Alex Atallah, previously likened the company to 'Stripe for AI,' providing a single access point for diverse AI systems and preventing vendor lock-in. The startup boasts 8 million global users and access to over 400 AI models.

The Wall Street Journal had reported on acquisition talks between Stripe and OpenRouter last month. While a Stripe spokesperson declined to comment on rumors or speculation, Bloomberg's report indicates the discussions have led to this substantial deal price.

headline_marked: [[OpenAI reportedly disbanded its preparedness team]] at end of last month, per FT
headline: OpenAI reportedly disbanded its preparedness team at end of last month, per FT
summary: The team was responsible for assessing and mitigating serious AI risks. This move is part of ongoing internal changes as the company prepares for an IPO.
details: According to the Financial Times, OpenAI reportedly disbanded its preparedness team at the end of last month. This team's primary role was to assess serious risks posed by AI models and develop mitigation strategies, such as preventing models from going rogue or hacking other companies.

Responsibility for these areas, including bio and cyber risks, has now been distributed among existing teams. This marks the latest in a series of organizational shifts within OpenAI as it moves towards an anticipated IPO.

Over the past few years, the company has also dissolved its AGI readiness and superalignment teams. Several key safety personnel, including ethics lead Chloé Bakalar and head of safety Johannes Heidecke, have recently departed.

Former OpenAI employee Jan Leike, who resigned in 2024, has criticized the company, telling the FT that it prioritizes "shiny products" over safety. The head of the disbanded preparedness team, Dylan Scandinaro, will now focus on the implications of "recursive self-improving" AI.
